open_points.subject: concurrent pointer publishes with one request id
open_points.text: “two publishes of a type get consecutive versions” versus “Two concurrent publishes of a type with different request ids are both accepted with consecutive versions” and “Two concurrent creates with one request id and equal facts ... make one record; the other answers it.”
open_points.question: When two concurrent publishes have the same request id and equal facts, do they create two consecutive pointer versions or one pointer with the other call answered as its repeat?
options: Create one pointer; the second call answers it as a repeat.
Create two pointers with consecutive versions.
open_points.default_guess: Create one pointer; the second call answers it as a repeat.

witness.initial: An active project has no pointer of type estimate; one publisher prepares two equal publish calls carrying the same request id.
events: Cabinet Kernel submits both publish calls concurrently for the same session and project.
The first transaction takes the store's write lock, creates version 1, and commits.
The second transaction takes the write lock and finds the first pointer carrying its request id.
outcomes: The second call is a repeat, so only version 1 exists and both calls answer that pointer.
The second call creates version 2, superseding version 1.
witness.observer: Cabinet Kernel and any caller listing or reading the project's pointers

open_points.subject: Customer value-form validation
open_points.text: “capability:customers.record_customer: (4) the request id's form, the name and kind required, the contact and fiscal data optional (A02)” and “capability:customers.correct_customer ... (4) the values” do not name capability:given_values.check_value_forms, although module:given_values now owns “a value outside its enumeration” and exports that capability.
open_points.question: Which operation invokes capability:given_values.check_value_forms for Customer kind and language during record and correction, and which operation converts its failures into the Customer's stage (4) refusal?
options: customers.record_customer and customers.correct_customer invoke it and return its failures at stage (4).
operations invokes it before calling customers.
customers duplicates the form checks without using the capability.
open_points.default_guess: customers.record_customer and customers.correct_customer invoke it and return its failures at stage (4).

open_points.subject: import mapping value-form validation
open_points.text: “module:migration_import owns reading the file, the mapping and its checks” and “capability:migration_import.read_import_mapping” are the only owner and operation named for mapping checks, while module:given_values now owns A02 rule 4 and exports capability:given_values.check_value_forms for failures that the import mapping must show.
open_points.question: Who calls capability:given_values.check_value_forms for the mapping's owner-given aliases and Customer values, and who turns its failures into mapping items that suppress the confirmation step?
options: migration_import.read_import_mapping calls given_values.check_value_forms and incorporates its failures into the mapping.
operations calls given_values.check_value_forms and combines its result with the mapping.
migration_import implements the checks itself despite given_values owning them.
open_points.default_guess: migration_import.read_import_mapping calls given_values.check_value_forms and incorporates its failures into the mapping.

set_aside.subject: stage (4) project-value failures
set_aside.text: “each one given within its form with capability:given_values.check_value_forms — the alias's length, the kind among its enumeration, the characteristics in range” but Errors lists only “Missing name or address, a malformed request id — stage (4), module:projects.”
set_aside.question: Which flow errors are produced when an alias is too long, an object kind is outside its enumeration, or a characteristic is outside its form?
options: Refuse at stage (4), naming every invalid value and its kind.
Treat these as an unspecified project refusal not represented in the Errors section.
Do not expose these failures as flow errors.
set_aside.default_guess: Refuse at stage (4), naming every invalid value and its kind, and add them to the Errors section.
